title: Drill 1: Precision Incision
brief: A clean incision is the first step of most operations, and a wandering or too-deep cut damages tissue that cannot be put back. Surgeons rehearse straight, even cuts on silicone pads long before they touch a patient.
objective: Trace the marked line from the green start dot to the end dot with the scalpel, keeping the blade on the line and at an even depth.
controls: Move the mouse to guide the scalpel over the pad
Hold the left mouse button to cut; release to lift the blade
Hold SHIFT for a steady breath: tremor drops, but your focus meter drains
scoring: Graded on average deviation from the line in millimetres (smaller is better), how consistent your cutting depth stays, and total time. Wandering more than 2 mm off the line flashes a red highlight and counts as an error.

title: Drill 2: Suturing
brief: Closing a wound means driving a curved needle through tissue at exactly the right entry and exit points, again and again. Poor needle handling tears tissue, so suturing is one of the first hands-on skills every surgical trainee must master.
objective: Pass the curved needle through each glowing entry and exit target pair, in order, without tearing the tissue.
controls: Move the mouse to position the needle driver
Hold the left mouse button and sweep along the needle's curve to drive it through the pad
Hold SHIFT for a steady breath: tremor drops, but your focus meter drains
scoring: Graded on how close each bite lands to its entry and exit targets (mm), tissue trauma from dragging or yanking the needle off its curve, and total time.

title: Drill 3: Laparoscopic Transfer
brief: In laparoscopy, instruments pass through small ports and the surgeon watches a 2D screen. The fulcrum effect reverses your hand motion at the tip, so this skill must be trained before operating. It is the idea behind peg transfer, a core task in the FLS program.
objective: Use the grasper to move all 3 pegs from the left posts to the right posts without touching the red vessels.
controls: Move the mouse: the tip moves the opposite way (fulcrum effect), pivoting at the port
Hold the left mouse button to close the jaws and grasp; release to let go
Hold SHIFT for a steady breath: tremor drops, but your focus meter drains
scoring: Graded on errors (vessel touches and dropped pegs), total time, and economy of motion (how short your tip's path is). Fewer errors, less time and a tighter path all score higher.
